title: Finance creatives that stay honest
summary: How to write and design loan, card, insurance and banking ads that are honest, approved and still convert, judged on what the lender actually pays for. You learn claims, angles, cost disclosure, formats, quality-based testing and the approval records that protect your payouts.

lessons.title: What finance ads can and cannot say
objectives: By the end you can sort any finance claim into benefit, promise or banned statement.
By the end you can explain why a misleading claim costs more per approved lead, with numbers.
By the end you can run a claim audit on an ad before it goes to the advertiser.

steps.h: Why claims decide your profit here
steps.p: In finance, one careless line can do three kinds of damage at once. The platform can reject the ad or restrict the account, the advertiser can cut you for brand or legal risk, and the people who click arrive expecting something the lender will not give. That last one shows up later as low approval and returned leads.

d.b: Every word in a finance ad is a promise someone checks
d.s: The platform, the lender, the regulator and the reader.

steps.say: Here's why claims decide your profit in finance. Look at the line on screen: every word in a finance ad is a promise someone checks. One careless line can do three kinds of damage at once. The platform can reject the ad or restrict the account. The advertiser can cut you for brand or legal risk. And the people who click arrive expecting something the lender won't give, which shows up later as low approval and returned leads.

steps.p: Before your ad earns a cent it passes four reviewers, whether you notice them or not. Each one can stop your campaign, and each one reads for something different. Writing for all four at once is the skill of this module.
d: Platform|ad policies, special ad categories, authorization
Law and regulator|cost disclosure, licences, fair marketing rules
Advertiser|brand rules, approved wording, banned phrases
The reader|is it true for someone like me?
steps.say: Before your ad earns a cent, it passes four reviewers. Look at the cards. The platform reads for ad policies, special ad categories and authorization. The law and the regulator read for cost disclosure, licences and fair marketing rules. The advertiser reads for brand rules, approved wording and banned phrases. And the reader asks: is this true for someone like me? Each one can stop your campaign, and writing for all four at once is the skill of this module.

steps.p: A promise states an outcome the lender controls, such as approval or a rate. You cannot make it. A benefit describes something true for every applicant, such as how long the form takes or that the full cost is shown before they accept. Write benefits.

a.title: Promises (remove)
items: Get N500,000 in your account today

b.title: Benefits (keep if true)
items: See the full cost before you accept
Decision usually the same day (lender's wording)

steps.say: Compare the two columns. On the left, promises to remove: guaranteed approval, everyone qualifies even with bad credit, get five hundred thousand naira in your account today, lowest rate in Nigeria. A promise states an outcome the lender controls, so you can't make it. On the right, benefits to keep, if true: check eligibility in about three minutes, see the full cost before you accept, compare offers from licensed lenders. A benefit describes something true for every applicant. So write benefits.

steps.p: Example rewrites. A rewrite is only safe if it is true for this offer and the advertiser approves it. 'Usually' and 'about' only belong in copy when the advertiser can back them with their own data.

rows: Checking won't affect your score (soft check)
Decision in minutes on most applications

steps.say: Here are some example rewrites. Look down the table. Guaranteed approval becomes check if you're eligible, because no lender can promise approval. No credit check becomes checking won't affect your score, if it's a soft check. Instant cash becomes decision in minutes on most applications. Free money becomes loan from a licensed lender, because loans are repaid. And zero percent interest needs its conditions, and the full terms. A rewrite is only safe if it's true for this offer and the advertiser approves it.

steps.h: Do not tell people what they are
steps.p: Meta's personal attributes rule says ad text must not assert or imply that you know a personal trait of the reader, and financial status is listed among them. 'Are you drowning in debt?' talks about the reader. 'How debt consolidation works' talks about the product. We are not certain this is current in every country; check Meta's Advertising Standards and the Help Center before relying on it.

d.b: Talk about the product, not the reader's money problems
d.s: Personal attributes policy. Check the current wording.

steps.p: Each wrong line guesses the reader's situation. Each right line describes what the product does, so it stays clear of the attribute rule and still speaks to the same need. The click intent is the same; the ad is safer.

steps.say: Let's rewrite the attribute out. On the left, each line guesses the reader's situation: struggling to pay rent this month, your credit score is bad, broke until payday. On the right, each line describes what the product does: short-term loans, see the cost before you apply. Products built for people building credit. Compare salary advance options and their fees. The click intent is the same, but the ad is safer.

steps.more: These summaries are deliberately simplified. US rules come from the Truth in Lending Act and Regulation Z, where 'trigger terms' such as a payment amount require further disclosures. UK consumer credit promotions follow the FCA's rules, which often require a representative example. Nigeria's FCCPC has issued digital lending regulations and Kenya's Central Bank licenses digital credit providers. Rules change and details matter, so treat this table as a reason to ask, not as the answer.

An interest rate or cost figure
A loan offer from a digital lender

steps.say: In several markets, putting certain cost details in an ad forces you to show more. Look at the table. In the United States, showing a monthly payment usually means adding the A P R, annual percentage rate, and repayment terms. In the United Kingdom, an interest rate usually needs a representative example with A P R. In Nigeria and Kenya, check the regulators' rules on cost disclosure. And in any geo, a rate or fee needs its conditions. These are simplified examples, not legal advice, so ask the advertiser's compliance team for the exact rule.

steps.h: Worked example: the cost of a promise
steps.p: Example: two ads, same $800 spend, same loan offer, payout on approval. The 'guaranteed' ad gets cheaper leads but the lender approves far fewer of them, because it attracted people the lender was never going to approve.
steps.more: Check the maths: $800 ÷ $0.80 = 1,000 leads. 4% of 1,000 = 40 approvals. $800 ÷ 40 = $20 each. Ad B: $800 ÷ $1.20 ≈ 667 leads. 12% of 667 ≈ 80 approvals. $800 ÷ 80 = $10 each. If the payout on approval is $15, Ad A loses $5 per approval and Ad B earns $5. Ad A also risks the account and the advertiser relationship. These are illustrative figures, not benchmarks.
steps.say: Here's a worked example: the cost of a promise. Two ads, the same eight hundred dollar spend, the same loan offer, paid on approval. Look at the table. Ad A, the guaranteed ad, gets leads at eighty cents, so one thousand leads, but only four percent are approved: forty approvals, at twenty dollars each. Ad B, the honest one, pays one dollar twenty per lead, but twelve percent are approved: about eighty approvals, at ten dollars each. With a fifteen dollar payout, A loses money and B earns. These are illustrative figures.

steps.p: Most rejected finance ads fail on the same handful of errors. Each one here has a simple fix you can apply before the ad is ever reviewed.

Bank or regulator logos|never imply endorsement you do not have
Figures without conditions|put the terms next to every number
Cash piles and fake alerts|no fake bank SMS or credit notifications
False urgency|'today only' must be true and approved
Skipping advertiser approval|get written sign-off every time
steps.say: Most rejected finance ads fail on the same handful of errors. Look at the cards. Copying a competitor ad: running isn't proof it's allowed, so audit it. Bank or regulator logos: never imply endorsement you don't have. Figures without conditions: put the terms next to every number. Cash piles and fake alerts: no fake bank S M S or credit notifications. False urgency: today only must be true and approved. And skipping advertiser approval: get written sign-off every time.

steps.p: Starting rules to adapt with your advertiser. They are deliberately strict because the cost of a wrong claim in finance is much higher than the cost of a slightly weaker ad.

rows: Ad shows a rate, payment or fee
Add the conditions or remove the figure
Stop that angle; ask for their approved list
Read the reason; fix; do not resubmit unchanged
Approval rate on an ad < 50% of account average

steps.say: Here are your starting rules for claims. If a claim has no written source, cut it before testing. If the ad shows a rate, payment or fee, add the conditions, or remove the figure. If the advertiser rejects a creative twice, stop that angle and ask for their approved list. If the platform rejects an ad, read the reason and fix it, and don't resubmit it unchanged. And if an ad's approval rate is under half the account average, pause it and re-check its claims. They're strict on purpose, because a wrong claim costs far more than a slightly weaker ad.

lessons.title: Honest angles that convert
objectives: By the end you can list six honest angles for loans, cards, insurance and banking.
By the end you can match an angle to a product and a stage of awareness.
By the end you can compare angles on cost per approval, not CTR.

steps.p: The angle is the reason you give someone to click. In finance it also decides who clicks. A 'fast cash' angle pulls urgent, often declined applicants. A 'compare the cost' angle pulls fewer, calmer people who more often qualify. The angle sets your approval rate before the form does.

d.s: And the lender's approval rate follows.

steps.say: The angle is the reason you give someone to click. In finance, it also decides who clicks. As the screen says, your angle chooses your applicants, and the lender's approval rate follows. A fast cash angle pulls urgent, often declined applicants. A compare the cost angle pulls fewer, calmer people who more often qualify. So the angle sets your approval rate before the form does.

steps.p: These angles work across loans, cards, insurance and accounts without promising outcomes. Each one gives a true reason to click. Pick the one that fits the product and the person's situation.
d: Speed of decision|how long the check takes, not approval
Cost transparency|see the total before you commit
Comparison|several licensed options side by side
Life event|school fees, new baby, car, moving
Education|how APR, credit scores or cover work
Tool|a calculator or eligibility checker
steps.say: Here are six honest finance angles. Look at the cards. Speed of decision: how long the check takes, not approval. Cost transparency: see the total before you commit. Comparison: several licensed options side by side. Life event: school fees, a new baby, a car, moving. Education: how A P R, the annual percentage rate, credit scores or cover work. And a tool: a calculator or eligibility checker. Each gives a true reason to click without promising outcomes.

steps.p: Example starting matches. They are not rules; test them. Note that insurance and bank accounts suit calmer, education-led angles, while short-term credit tempts buyers into urgency angles that bring weak applicants.
steps.say: Which angle fits which product? These are example starting matches, not rules, so test them. Look down the table. For a personal loan, use cost transparency or a tool, and avoid fast cash. For a credit card, comparison or rewards explained, and avoid approval for all. For insurance, life event or comparison, not fear of disaster. For a bank or savings app, education and fees compared, never get rich or free money. And for debt consolidation, one payment with total cost shown, never debt-shaming.

steps.p: People arrive at different stages. Someone who has never compared loans needs education first. Someone who already knows what they want needs proof and a clear next step. Write the first line for the stage you are targeting.
d: Unaware of options
Problem-aware
Comparing products
Ready to apply
steps.say: People arrive at different stages of awareness. Look at the funnel. In this example, one thousand people are unaware of their options, six hundred are problem-aware, two hundred and fifty are comparing products, and only eighty are ready to apply. Someone who has never compared loans needs education first. Someone who already knows what they want needs proof and a clear next step. So write your first line for the stage you're targeting.

steps.h: Example: the angle in plain words
steps.p: Example of a calm comparison angle in a chat-style creative. It explains, shows cost, and leaves the decision to the reader. Nothing is promised, and every figure comes from the offer's terms.

d.text: How much would a N200,000 loan actually cost me?
It depends on the lender and term. On this offer's example terms, 3 months at the stated rate, you would repay about N236,000 in total.
Yes, on those example terms. You see your exact cost before you accept, and you can say no.

steps.say: Here's a calm comparison angle in a chat-style creative, an example. The reader asks how much a two hundred thousand naira loan would actually cost. The answer explains it depends on the lender and term, and on this offer's example terms, three months at the stated rate, they'd repay about two hundred and thirty six thousand naira in total. Then it confirms the extra cost, and says you see your exact cost before you accept, and you can say no. Nothing is promised, and every figure comes from the offer's terms.

steps.p: Example: $300 per angle, payout $12 per approved credit card application. Compare the last column only. CTR and CPL alone would have picked the wrong winner.
steps.more: Check the maths. Fast approval: $300 ÷ $1.50 = 200 leads; 6% = 12 approvals; $300 ÷ 12 = $25.00. Rewards: $300 ÷ $2.50 = 120 leads; 18% = 21.6 approvals; $300 ÷ 21.6 ≈ $13.89. Compare: $300 ÷ $2.00 = 150 leads; 20% = 30 approvals; $300 ÷ 30 = $10.00. With a $12 payout only 'Compare 3 cards' is profitable. Illustrative figures, not benchmarks.
steps.say: Here's a worked example: three angles, three hundred dollars each, with a twelve dollar payout per approved credit card application. Look only at the last column. Fast approval had the cheapest leads, at one fifty, but only six percent were approved, so twenty five dollars per approval. Rewards explained came to about thirteen eighty nine. Compare three cards had twenty percent approval, so ten dollars per approval. With a twelve dollar payout, only compare three cards is profitable. C T R, click-through rate, and C P L alone would have picked the wrong winner. These are illustrative figures.

steps.h: Lab: most you can pay per lead
steps.p: Use the breakeven lab. Payout is $12 per approved application, 20% of leads are approved, and you keep a 25% margin. What is the most you can pay per lead and still hit your target?

steps.say: Here are starting rules for angle tests. Target means your target cost per paid event. If spend reaches two times target with zero paid events, kill the angle. If cost per paid event is at or below zero point eight times target, with three or more events, keep it, and make three new hooks on it. If C P L is good but approval is under half of average, pause, because the angle attracts the wrong applicants. And if approval data isn't back yet, hold, and don't judge on C P L alone. Use the network's approval data, not your own form count.

steps.h: Why cost clarity pays you back
steps.p: People who see the full cost before applying are less likely to drop out at the offer stage, complain or default. Lenders notice. Affiliates who send informed applicants often get better approval rates and are trusted with better deals. Hiding cost buys clicks today and costs you the partner later.

steps.h: The cost words beginners mix up
steps.p: These terms appear on every loan offer. You must understand them to write honest copy and to spot an offer you should not promote. Ask the advertiser for each figure in writing.
d: Interest rate|price of borrowing, per period
Fees|origination, service or late fees
APR|yearly cost including some fees
Total repayable|everything the borrower pays back
Term|how long until fully repaid
steps.say: These cost words appear on every loan offer, and beginners mix them up. Look at the cards. The interest rate is the price of borrowing, per period. Fees can be origination, service or late fees. A P R, the annual percentage rate, is the yearly cost including some fees. Total repayable is everything the borrower pays back. And the term is how long until it's fully repaid. Understand these to write honest copy, and ask the advertiser for each figure in writing.

steps.p: The simplest honest figure is the total the borrower will pay back. It is easy to understand and hard to disguise. Many regulators ask for it, and readers grasp it faster than a rate.

steps.say: The simplest honest figure is the total repayable. Read the equation: amount borrowed, plus interest, plus fees, equals total repayable. It's easy to understand, and hard to disguise. Many regulators ask for it, and readers grasp it faster than a rate.

steps.p: Example terms, not a real offer: N100,000 for 3 months, 5% flat interest per month, a 2% one-off fee. Work out what the borrower actually repays and the cost for every N1 borrowed.
steps.more: A flat 5% per month sounds small. Over a year that pattern would be 60% in simple interest before fees, and the true APR on a loan you pay down monthly is higher still, because you pay interest on money you have already partly repaid. Calculating an exact APR needs the lender's method and is the lender's job. Your job is to show the figures the lender gives you, with their conditions, and never to show only the friendliest one.
steps.say: Here's a worked example, with example terms, not a real offer. One hundred thousand naira for three months, at five percent flat interest per month, plus a two percent one-off fee. That's seventeen kobo of cost for every naira borrowed. A flat five percent a month sounds small, but the true A P R is much higher, and calculating it is the lender's job, not yours.
